article.title: Cursor Launches Origin Code-Hosting Platform, Then Watches a Six-Hour GitHub Outage Hit It on Day One
article.summary: Cursor's new GitHub-rival hosting platform went into beta the same day a six-hour GitHub outage knocked out the feature it depends on.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Cursor, the AI coding-tool maker that officially became part of SpaceX earlier this month, began rolling out Origin, a new code-hosting platform designed to compete with GitHub, in early beta on paid plans starting August 17, according to [Cursor's own changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting). Hours after the launch, Cursor's status page reported that Origin itself was degraded by a GitHub-side outage, according to [Cursor's incident report](https://status.cursor.com/incidents/l9h9vrd726jv).

## What We Know

Origin lets developers "host your code" inside Cursor's own infrastructure rather than solely on GitHub, with support for repositories, pull requests, and code browsing, according to [Cursor's changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting). The rollout covers all paid plans except enterprise organizations whose administrators opt out; free-tier users are not included, per the same changelog.

Origin does not require developers to abandon GitHub. "Your GitHub repos can sit alongside the ones Cursor hosts. Connect GitHub to Cursor, pick your org, and you'll see the repos you can sync," Cursor wrote in the changelog. Synced repositories update in real time inside Origin, but GitHub remains "the source of truth for anything started there," and pull-request comments sync both ways within seconds, so a review assigned on GitHub can be completed from inside Cursor. Icons next to each repository indicate whether it is hosted by Cursor or pulled in from GitHub.

Cursor is also building an "app ecosystem" around Origin, with integrations already available for Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite, and says "agent-native" features are coming soon but has not detailed them yet, according to both [Cursor's changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog/origin-code-hosting) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/18/cursor-capitalizes-on-github-frustration-launches-rival-hosting-platform/).

The timing drew attention because Origin's debut coincided with a GitHub outage. "On the same day that Cursor launched its new platform, GitHub suffered a quite lengthy worldwide outage. For over six hours, the site's functions were reportedly degraded, with a nearly 20% error rate worldwide," [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/18/cursor-capitalizes-on-github-frustration-launches-rival-hosting-platform/). Cursor's own status page confirms the disruption reached its own products: an incident titled "GitHub degradation affecting some Cursor services — Automations, Cloud Agents, Codebase" opened at 14:34 UTC on August 17, attributed the problem to "a GitHub degradation reported in GitHub's status page," and was marked resolved at 20:40 UTC, roughly six hours later, according to [Cursor's incident report](https://status.cursor.com/incidents/l9h9vrd726jv). That report lists Origin itself among the affected components, alongside Automations, Review Agents, and Cloud Agents.

The outage was not an isolated incident. Between May 2025 and April 2026, the incident-monitoring service IncidentHub tracked 257 separate incidents on GitHub, of which 48 were classified as major outages — roughly one significant disruption per week — with GitHub's Actions CI/CD system alone suffering 57 outages over that period, according to [LeadDev](https://leaddev.com/software-quality/whats-gone-wrong-at-github). LeadDev, whose analysis TechCrunch cited in its coverage of the Origin launch, wrote that the reliability problems have "triggered a visible exodus of high-profile users."

GitHub remains far larger than any prospective rival. "According to GitHub's own metrics, some 180 million developers use its platform as of last October," [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/18/cursor-capitalizes-on-github-frustration-launches-rival-hosting-platform/), noting that the platform was founded in 2007 and acquired by Microsoft in 2012.

## What We Don't Know

Cursor has not published pricing details for Origin or a timeline for the "agent-native" features it says are coming. Cursor also has not said whether the August 17 outage affected Origin users' ability to sync or access repositories, only that Origin was among the components its status page listed as affected. The company has not given a target date for when Origin might exit beta or become available to free-tier users.

## Analysis

Origin's launch places Cursor, now backed by SpaceX's resources following the [acquisition that closed on August 14](/article/2026-08/17-spacex-closes-60-billion-acquisition-of-cursor-completing-the-deal-it-struck-in-june), in direct competition with the code-hosting incumbent it currently depends on for synced repositories. The design keeps GitHub as the default source of truth for existing projects, a structure that lets Cursor court developers frustrated with GitHub's reliability without forcing an immediate migration. The same-day outage that touched Origin itself illustrates the dependency Cursor is trying to loosen: even a platform built to offer an alternative to GitHub was not insulated from GitHub's problems on its first day live.
